findings: A second agent session on the same machine, sharing this working tree and the VPS, developed the same tooling concurrently and rewrote tools mid-run (three tools at 21:02:19Z, 19 s before an evidence run). Sixteen-plus P11 runs between 17:00 and 20:50Z are not attributable to this stream and disagree with it on NC results. The byte set was therefore frozen and every required run re-executed afterwards. Failure record 20261019T2135Z.

NC1 in the first frozen-byte NC run was invalidated by a foreign sik_p6f fixture re-created 46 s after a teardown; the NC driver reuses an existing fixture. A clean re-run discriminates. The driver's fixture-reuse behaviour is a latent defect and is not fixed in the frozen candidate.

An ad-hoc live-proof hash computed by this stream used a tab join and printed 356355:424624d9...; the canonical pipe-join recipe gives 356355:a66a3a54... on the same data. No live change; the wrong value was discarded, not reported as a state change.
Earlier P11 evidence (NC 5/5 at 13:56Z, suite 39/39 at 15:10Z, preservation PASS at 15:32Z) was produced by tool bytes that no longer exist; it is retained in evidence/p11/ but not relied on.
live_state_post: databases sik, sik_bench; both database.xml copies on sik; ledger 356,355 rows, content a66a3a54...; no .writer_exclusion_* marker; no benchmark grant on sik_p6f. Note: at 01:21:07Z the other session had re-created sik_p6f with a benchmark grant; the clean point immediately after this stream's last mutating run (01:07:40Z) and the 21:12:34Z proof are the evidence, both quoted in section 22.
